summary.headline: Finkurve Q2 FY27: AUM up about 95% YoY, ROE above 10% at 2.5x+ leverage, while gold-loan NPAs rose and collection efficiency fell to about 90%.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as one of its best quarters on profitability, with operating profit up 62% YoY, total income up about 88% and branch count at 122 versus 92 a year earlier. Growth slowed sequentially, with AUM up about 3% QoQ versus about 16% in Q1 and over 30% in Q4, which management called a transition rather than a slowdown. Reported NPAs rose and collection efficiency fell to around 90% from about 98%, which management attributed to the shift from bullet repayment to periodic repayment under the new RBI framework and to gold price correction. Off-book co-lending grew sharply, with its share of AUM rising from about 1-3% to about 6%.

segments.name: Gold loans (on-book)
segments.commentary: Management says 90% of the personal-loan-plus-gold mix is secured gold lending. Yields rose to 20.8% from 20%, and management says yield gains, not one-time items, drove the revenue rise.

segments.name: Personal loans (unsecured, via digital lending partners/NBFC-P2P-type partners)
segments.commentary: Portfolio averages about Rs 45-50 crore per quarter and is about 10% of the mix. Tickets range from Rs 5,000 to Rs 2 lakh (average about Rs 20,000), tenure 15 days to about 36 months; management aims for a higher share over time.

segments.name: Off-book co-lending
segments.commentary: Off-book AUM roughly doubled to about Rs 7,000 crore in the quarter, and management says almost all of the sequential AUM growth came from gold co-lending partners. Target: 30-35% of the overall book in 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 50-60% reiterated; management sees no current concern in reaching it.
Branch additions of 50-60 guided earlier, now 60-70 for FY27; about 150 branches by December 2026 (about 28 more) and further expansion through March 2027.
Off-book share to reach 30-35% of the overall book in about three years.
Expects NIM to rise as cost of funds falls and cost-to-income ratio to fall as branch AUM grows; expects more co-lending partners by end FY27.
Renewals expected to fall to about 10-15% at current prices, versus 60-65% when prices were high.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 122, adding about 28 more by December 2026 and further openings through March 2027.
Two co-lending partners live; one more to go live in Q3 FY27 and a revived partner in Q4 FY27; more partners targeted by end FY27.
Cash-flow-based lending training and system changes under way; management says this will take time.
demand_pricing: Competition: management says there is no product differentiation from banks and large NBFCs; it focuses on tier-2/3 customers with limited bank access, and says yields are higher as a result.
Gold price correction reduced loan demand because customers realise lower amounts on the same gold; renewals have dropped as a result.
Average ticket size declining consciously because of the new LTV schemes; customer retention at maturity above 60%.
LTV has increased, with management citing the RBI allowing up to 85% LTV for consumption loans and prices correcting, and says it still sees no incremental risk.
Management says informal lenders are losing share (about 60-40 split moving toward 65-35) as banks restrict repledging.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company differentiate from banks and large gold NBFCs?
qa_highlights.answer: No product differentiation; it targets customers with limited bank access in tier-2/3 cities. Competitive edge is turnaround time, scheme design and pricing together.

qa_highlights.question: What drove revenue up about 20% QoQ with AUM up only 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold yields rose from 20% to 20.8% and co-lending share rose to about 5.8%. Management says there was no one-time income.

qa_highlights.question: Plan to reduce NCD reliance (about 57% of borrowings)?
qa_highlights.answer: No fresh NCDs in Q2; NCD cost is now on par with bank borrowings. NCDs are capped at 40-45% of borrowings, and bank sanctions are in hand.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NPAs rise and how will stressed assets be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it to the shift to periodic repayment and regulatory changes, and says gold loan NPAs carry low credit loss because of borrower equity. Auction is a last resort; management expects recovery over 1-2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AUM growth slow to about 3% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management calls it a transition, citing regulation, gold price correction (lower loan amounts) and intense competition. It still expects 50-60% annual growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI gold loan directions on documentation and LTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Documentation now includes business registration and income documents for loans above Rs 2.5 lakh. Cash-flow-based lending is at an early stage; management says it will raise credit risk and needs staff training.

risks_watch: Collection efficiency fell to about 90% from about 98%, and NPAs rose; watch the reported NPA figure and recovery pace next quarter.
Rising LTV (up to 85%) and cash-flow-based lending under new RBI rules may raise credit costs; management concedes this.
Growth moderated sharply (AUM +3% QoQ); watch whether 50-60% annual growth guidance holds.
Gold price volatility and competition from banks and large NBFCs.
Funding: NCDs about 57% of borrowings; bank share and new co-lending partners need to deliver cheaper funding.
Management declined to comment on share price weakness; the stock has lagged reported growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, profitability and branch expansion, but defensive on asset quality. On NPAs and collection efficiency, management relied on collateral equity arguments. It also gave vague answers on share price and did not give several requested figures (renewal data, LTV split), offering to send them after the call.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects NIM to rise as cost of funds falls, with gold yield up to 20.8% from 20% QoQ, though collection efficiency fell to about 90% from 98% and credit costs may rise.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network at 122 with about 28 more firmly planned to reach ~150 by December 2026 (Q3 FY27), and 60-70 additions guided for FY27 (4 added in Q2, 13 in Q1).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM guidance of 50-60% for FY27 was reiterated, but AUM grew only about 3% QoQ in Q2 versus about 16% in Q1, and gold price correction is cutting loan sizes.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held at 50-60% AUM growth, and Q2 AUM growth of about 3% QoQ and rising NPAs argue against an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: AUM grew only about 3% QoQ, collection efficiency fell to about 90% from 98%, and reported NPAs rose (analyst cited about 2.4% to 2.6%, unconfirmed), so the 50-60% growth target is at risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management aims for a higher personal-loan share over time and is adding co-lending partners (one live in Q3 FY27, a revived partner in Q4 FY27), but no specific product launch date was given.

rows.label: Off-book co-lending scale-up to 30-35% of book
rows.why: Off-book AUM roughly doubled to about Rs 7,000 crore (share about 6% from 1-3%), with one more partner going live in Q3 FY27 and a revived partner in Q4 FY27; target is 30-35% of the book in about three years.

rows.label: Shift away from NCD funding
rows.why: NCDs are about 57% of borrowings against a 40-45% cap, no fresh NCDs were raised in Q2, and bank sanctions are in hand, but the cap is not yet reached.

rows.label: Gold loan renewals recovery
rows.why: Renewals are expected to fall to about 10-15% at current prices from 60-65% when prices were high, and the gold price correction is reducing loan amounts.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, profitability and branch expansion but defensive on asset quality, relying on collateral-equity arguments for NPAs and collection efficiency; analysts pushed on the 3% QoQ AUM slowdown, the NPA rise, and the lack of concrete figures.
